tagline: Off the little ferry and up under the castle.
intro: Off the ferry from Chester, Route 148 runs 1.6 miles east through Hadlyme, a village named for Haddam and Lyme because it straddles the line between them, to Route 82 at the Four Corners, where an old carriage factory now sells antiques. From there a side road goes north past Gillette Castle, and Route 156 heads south through Hamburg toward Old Lyme.
The crossing began in 1769, when Jonathan Warner, who owned land on both banks, put a raft to work with long poles. In the Revolution it carried supplies over the Connecticut.

moments.title: Chester-Hadlyme Ferry
moments.text: The Selden III takes eight or nine cars across in about five minutes, and anyone on the Hadlyme side calls it over by pushing a button that flashes a light.

moments.title: Gillette Castle
moments.text: William Gillette, the stage Sherlock Holmes, found these cliffs from his houseboat and built a fieldstone castle on top, then willed that no "blithering sap-head" should ever have it.

moments.title: Hamburg
moments.text: About 1824 a deep-water channel was dredged up to Hamburg, the village center of Lyme, and the older landing upriver at Hamburg Bridge began to fade.

practical: The ferry runs in daylight from April 1 to November 30 only.
